package_info.package_manager: Microsoft SQL Server (Extended Stored Procedure DLL)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (DLL-based, not versioned in a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The Maggie DLL is a backdoor that, once loaded as an Extended Stored Procedure in Microsoft SQL Server, allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands, interact with the filesystem, brute-force logins to other MSSQL servers, create new backdoor users, and establish network proxies and port forwarding. This enables full remote control and lateral movement within the victim's environment.

execution_context.file_location: Loaded as an Extended Stored Procedure DLL in MSSQL server

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code receives a command via a SQL query, executes the command on the underlying OS, and returns the output to the attacker, enabling remote command execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing arbitrary OS command execution from SQL queries is highly dangerous and not a standard feature of legitimate stored procedures.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal extended stored procedures should not provide unrestricted OS command execution to remote users.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some administrative tools may allow limited command execution for maintenance, but never in an unrestricted, unauthenticated manner.
key_indicators: Arbitrary command execution via SQL interface
Returns command output to remote user

execution_context.file_location: Loaded as an Extended Stored Procedure DLL in MSSQL server

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attempts to brute-force administrator logins on remote MSSQL servers and, upon success, creates a new backdoor user with hardcoded credentials, enabling persistent unauthorized access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Brute-forcing logins and creating unauthorized users are clear indicators of malicious lateral movement and persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate stored procedures should not attempt to brute-force other servers or create unauthorized users.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; brute-forcing and backdoor user creation are always malicious in this context.
key_indicators: Automated brute-force of remote MSSQL servers

execution_context.file_location: Loaded as an Extended Stored Procedure DLL in MSSQL server

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code starts a SOCKS5 proxy server on the infected MSSQL server, enabling attackers to tunnel arbitrary network traffic through the compromised host.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Enabling a SOCKS5 proxy on a database server is highly abnormal and facilitates covert lateral movement and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Database servers should not act as network proxies or bridgeheads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, proxies may be used for debugging, but never on production database servers without strict controls.
key_indicators: SOCKS5 proxy functionality in a database extension

execution_context.file_location: Loaded as an Extended Stored Procedure DLL in MSSQL server

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sets up TCP port forwarding on the infected server, redirecting incoming connections to a designated IP and port if the source IP matches a user-specified mask, enabling covert access to internal resources.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Port forwarding from a database server is highly unusual and enables attackers to bypass network segmentation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Database servers should not provide arbitrary port forwarding or act as network bridgeheads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Port forwarding may be used in controlled admin scenarios, but never exposed via a backdoor.
key_indicators: Source IP mask for selective redirection

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads and loads the Maggie DLL as an Extended Stored Procedure on the MSSQL server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor is installed and ready to receive commands.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues SQL queries to execute arbitrary OS commands via the backdoor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote command execution on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the backdoor to brute-force logins to other MSSQL servers and creates new backdoor users.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves lateral movement and persistence in the environment.

attack_chain.action: Attacker enables SOCKS5 proxy or port forwarding to tunnel network traffic through the compromised server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker establishes covert network access to internal resources.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual invocation of extended stored procedures with command execution parameters
Creation of new SQL users with hardcoded or suspicious credentials
MSSQL server initiating brute-force login attempts to other servers
Database server listening on unexpected ports (SOCKS5, port forwarding)
Database server acting as a network proxy or bridgehead
file_indicators: DLLs named sql64.dll or similar in MSSQL extension directories
RAR SFX archives containing Maggie DLLs
network_indicators: Unexpected SOCKS5 or port forwarding traffic from MSSQL server
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the loading of unknown or suspicious DLLs as extended stored procedures in MSSQL servers. Alert on the creation of new SQL users with unusual or hardcoded credentials. Detect brute-force login attempts originating from MSSQL servers to other MSSQL instances. Monitor for unexpected network listeners (SOCKS5, port forwarding) or outbound connections to known malicious IPs/domains. Correlate with known file hashes and filenames associated with Maggie.
